Requirement: Management has approved an implementation plan, with timelines, for the requirements of SEBON IT Policy 2083 that apply to the organization.
Responsibility for IT policy implementation and monitoring is assigned to a named function or committee with periodic reporting to senior management.
A Business Process Re-engineering (BPR) assessment is planned or performed every three years, covering digitization of licensing, regulatory reporting and surveillance-related processes.
The organization tracks and complies with the minimum IT Standard issued by SEBON for licensed entities.
The organizational structure includes a defined IT/IS function with adequate staffing for IT, resources and personnel management.
An Information Security Management System (ISMS) based on ISO/IEC 27001, or an equivalent standard approved by SEBON, is implemented.
The ISMS is ISO/IEC 27001 certified.
The organization complies with the minimum cyber security baseline prescribed by SEBON for market participants.
Information security roles, responsibilities and a cyber security awareness program are in place for staff.
Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) is enforced before sensitive information is transmitted or accessed in regulatory, trading, depository and intermediary service systems.
Regulatory documents, reports and disclosures submitted to SEBON are digitally signed.
Digital signature certificates in use are issued by a CA licensed under the Controller of Certification Authorities (CCA) or a CA recognized by SEBON.
Digital signatures are used, or planned, for investor-broker agreements and KYC processes.
APIs exposed to third parties enforce authentication and authorization controls.
APIs exposed to third parties enforce request rate limiting.
API traffic is encrypted using TLS 1.2 or higher, with weaker protocols disabled.
API activity is logged, retained and reviewed.
APIs comply with the API security standard prescribed by SEBON.
Vendor due diligence is performed before onboarding third-party IT service providers, including cloud providers.
An ongoing vendor risk management process exists (inventory, risk rating, periodic review) for third-party IT service providers.
IT outsourcing contracts include a Service Level Agreement (SLA) with measurable service levels.
IT outsourcing contracts define data security, confidentiality and liability obligations of the vendor.
IT outsourcing contracts grant audit and inspection rights, including regulatory audit rights.
IT outsourcing contracts include a documented vendor exit strategy.
Cloud computing is formally evaluated as an option when procuring IT equipment and services.
A Business Continuity Plan (BCP) is documented and approved.
A Disaster Recovery Plan (DRP) is documented and approved.
BCP and DRP are tested at least annually (drill or simulation) and the test report is submitted to SEBON.
Recovery Time Objective (RTO) and Recovery Point Objective (RPO) are clearly defined for critical systems.
The Disaster Recovery Site is located at least 25 km from the primary site.
A multi-layered backup strategy protects sensitive data and systems from ransomware, malware, cyber attack and accidental modification or deletion.
Immutable snapshots are used as part of the backup strategy.
Air-gapped backups are maintained.
VAPT of critical systems is conducted at least annually.
VAPT reports are submitted to SEBON within three months of test completion.
Critical vulnerabilities identified in VAPT are remediated within 30 days.
IT/system audit is conducted annually.
IT/system audit is conducted at least every two years.
IT audit scope covers, at minimum, trading systems, clearing and settlement, cyber security controls, BCP/DRP and data management.
IT audit reports are submitted to SEBON within three months.
Critical audit findings are remediated within 30 days.
Defined standards are applied for software development or acquisition, technical evaluation and pre-delivery inspection.
IT auditor selection follows the System Audit Framework and auditor selection norms issued by SEBON.
24x7 cyber threat monitoring is in place through an in-house Security Operations Centre (SOC) or a recognized Managed Security Service Provider (MSSP).
An Incident Response Plan (IRP) is prepared and submitted to SEBON.
Cyber incidents directly affecting market operations are reported to SEBON on the same day.
Other significant cyber incidents are reported to SEBON within 72 hours.
A Root Cause Analysis (RCA) report is submitted to SEBON within 30 days of an incident.
Incidents are reported through the integrated capital market cyber incident reporting portal.
Data is classified into SEBON categories: public data, sensitive business data and personal investor data.
Securities market data is stored within Nepal (data localization).
Data centres used are IDMC or data centres officially listed with the Department of Information Technology, Government of Nepal.
A Data Lifecycle Management Policy is implemented.
Electronic filing to SEBON is done through SEDFAR with digital signatures.
Algorithmic trading systems are approved by the stock exchange before use (mark N/A if not used).
AI/ML systems used in trading, surveillance or investor services have mandatory human oversight (human-in-the-loop). Mark N/A if not used.
Decisions made by AI systems are explainable and documented (Explainable AI). Mark N/A if not used.
